startups.name: Skyline Drones
startups.description: Delivers parcels across the city with a fleet of small autonomous drones. Founded by two ex-airline engineers.

news.text: The regulator opens a pilot air corridor for delivery drones.
A rival's drone crashes into a stadium and the press demands stricter rules. Skyline's fleet is untouched.
Skyline is shortlisted for a national supermarket contract.

insiders.text: The pilot corridor is fully booked: expect profit per share to roughly double.
A partner retailer has tripled its drone order for the quarter.
Stricter rules will hit the rivals harder. Expect a solid rise of about three.
Two large retailers are switching to Skyline this turn.
The supermarket deal is signed, but deliveries start late. Only a small rise of about two.
Insiders say the contract is worth around two extra units per share.

startups.name: BloodSense
startups.description: A pocket device that analyses your blood from a single finger prick and sends the result to your phone.

news.text: Tech blogs call the finger-prick analyser a breakthrough. Pre-orders are exploding.
A hospital study questions how accurate the sensor really is.
The health regulator announces an investigation into BloodSense.

insiders.text: Pre-orders are far above plan: expect a jump of about five.
The test results are much worse than the company admits. Expect a clear drop of about three.
Several clinics are quietly cancelling their orders.
A sales halt is coming. The company will earn nothing this turn.
Investors are pulling out. The profit will fall to zero.

startups.name: GreenCrate
startups.description: A weekly subscription box of seasonal vegetables from local farms, delivered in reusable crates.

news.text: A quiet quarter: subscriptions hold steady.
A well-received ad campaign brings in a few new subscribers.
Two competitors copy the idea, but loyal customers stay.

insiders.text: No surprises: profit stays exactly where it was.
Sign-ups are up modestly. Expect a rise of one.
Profit stays flat as the new competitors take a few customers.
Nothing dramatic: the same profit as last turn.

startups.name: PixelPals
startups.description: An indie studio building a cosy online game where players raise tiny digital pets.

news.text: A teaser trailer goes viral and the waiting list passes a million.
The launch is buggy and reviews are harsh.
A big patch and a free expansion win players back.

insiders.text: Expect a big jump of about five as the waiting list converts to buyers.
Servers are crashing under load. Expect a fall of about four.
Refund requests are piling up.
The expansion is a hit: expect a rise of about five.
Players are returning in large numbers.

startups.name: NanoFarm
startups.description: Vertical farms inside empty city warehouses, growing salad leaves under LED light.

news.text: Construction delays push the first harvest back.
The first harvest sells out within a week.
Two restaurant chains sign long-term supply deals.

insiders.text: The delay costs nothing yet: profit stays the same.
Demand is far above supply. Expect a jump of about four.
Buyers are queuing for the first crates.
Supply deals add roughly two units per share.
A modest rise: the new contracts only start late in the turn.

startups.name: SafeLock Wallet
startups.description: A hardware wallet that keeps companies' digital payment keys offline and tamper-proof.

news.text: A steady quarter with the usual corporate customers.
A rival launches a cheaper alternative.
Several big customers announce they are switching suppliers.

insiders.text: Nothing changes: the profit stays the same.
Price pressure is real. Expect a fall of about two.
The rival's product is getting excellent reviews.
The customer losses are larger than the company admits: expect a fall of about two.
Profit will be close to one.
